analysis.investment_thesis: Alivus is a high-quality API manufacturer with exceptional margins (31% operating, 55% gross) and an essentially debt-free balance sheet, but recent profit growth has stalled at ~3% YoY (INR 471 Cr → 486 Cr), making the current P/E of 37.3x extremely hard to justify. The story only becomes interesting if new ownership (Nirma) can credibly re-accelerate earnings toward the implied forward P/E of 21x.
key_strengths: Fortress balance sheet — D/E of 0.02, fortress-level; ROCE of 23.3% signals exceptional capital efficiency
Premium margins for an API player — 31.4% operating margin and 55% gross margin are best-in-class and durable
Diversified API portfolio across high-value therapeutic areas (oncology, CNS, cardiovascular) with global export reach
key_risks: Growth has decelerated sharply — net profit essentially flat for 3 years (INR 419→467→471→486 Cr), making 37x P/E indefensible on a PEG basis (PEG ~2.3)
Large mystery deployment in FY2025 — investing CF of -616 Cr dwarfs capex of -166 Cr; the remaining ~450 Cr allocation is unexplained and cash dropped from 301 to 71 Cr
Ownership/brand transition risk — renamed from Glenmark Life Sciences to Alivus under Nirma in Dec 2024; execution track record under new parent is unproven
red_flags: PEG ratio ~2.3x on current P/E (37.3 / 16% 6Y CAGR) — well above Lynch's 1.0 ceiling; even using forward P/E of 21 and assuming 20% growth, PEG is still ~1.05
Revenue growth has slowed to ~7% YoY (2024-2025) vs. 17.6% 6Y CAGR — the historical CAGR is misleading; the recent trend tells a stagnation story
Free cash flow declining trend: INR 465 Cr (2022) → 143 → 285 → 225 Cr (2025); OCF of 392 Cr in 2025 barely covers capex + big investment outflows
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Lynch GARP standpoint, Alivus passes the quality test but fails the price test badly. The business is genuinely excellent — operating margins of 31.4% are extraordinary for an API manufacturer, ROCE of 23.3% signals real competitive advantage in process chemistry, and D/E of 0.02 means zero financial risk. The product mix (olmesartan, sitagliptin, oncology APIs like palbociclib/cabozantinib) is moving up the value chain. I can understand the business: it makes the ingredients inside branded pills and sells globally. Simple story. But the numbers don't support the price.

The PEG ratio is the deal-breaker. At P/E 37.3x divided by my preferred growth rate (I'd use the recent 3-year profit trend, not the 6Y CAGR), the PEG blows out to 3x+. Even on the 6Y CAGR of 16.3%, PEG is 2.3 — I start sweating above 1.5. The forward P/E of 21.14 is intriguing and implies a near-doubling of earnings; if Nirma-backed CDMO scale-up delivers that, the stock is a bargain today. But I need to see the growth before I pay for it. The massive 2025 investing outflow (₹616 Cr) could be the catalyst for re-acceleration — or it could be capital misallocation. Until the story clarifies under new ownership, this is a HOLD for existing investors and a pass for new money.
